sources.title: HN: Writing a good Claude.md (thread on HumanLayer post)
sources.note: Whole 349-line thread read. Top comments describe the post as: keep CLAUDE.md short and universally applicable; Claude ignores it as it grows (system-reminder says may not be relevant); ~150-200 instruction budget with decay as count rises; progressive disclosure via separate task docs; do not use an LLM as linter/formatter; do not auto-generate it. Instruction-count plot uses models over 6 months old (commenters note). Commenters cross-check: post author 0xblacklight (Kyle) and dhorthy (Dex) both reply.

sources.title: OrcaBot: Do Skills Improve Coding Agent Accuracy?
sources.note: Fully read. Third-party (Rob Macrae). Codex 5.5 (gpt-5.5, high effort), Codex CLI v0.136.0, NOT Claude. Five skill packs vs no-skill baseline on SWE-bench Pro (729-731 instances, 1 seed) and SlopCodeBench (36 problems/196 checkpoints, n=3 seeds). June and July runs. Does not cite Dex directly; relevant as a measurement against skills/instruction-heavy workflows and the SlopCodeBench benchmark Dex reported on.

cards.source_title: OrcaBot: Do Skills Improve Coding Agent Accuracy?
cards.author: other
cards.quote: the public workflow skills mostly wash.
cards.claim: Measured against a contemporaneous no-skill baseline, five public skill packs mostly produce no reliable accuracy gain on SWE-bench Pro or SlopCodeBench.
cards.evidence_detail: Codex 5.5 high; July SWE-bench Pro (729 instances, 1 seed): OMC +1.65, Superpowers-v6 +1.51, Karpathy +0.96, GSD -0.14, Agent Skills -1.10 vs 55.56% baseline; all gaps under 2 points.
cards.landing: Evidence to weigh before adding workflow skills under .claude/skills/: skills should be measured against a no-skill baseline on this repo's own tasks, not assumed helpful.

cards.source_title: OrcaBot: Do Skills Improve Coding Agent Accuracy?
cards.author: other
cards.quote: On SlopCodeBench, no: every skill collection actively hurt.
cards.claim: In the June run every skill pack scored below the Codex 5.5 baseline on SlopCodeBench Strict, while all beat baseline on SWE-bench Pro.
cards.evidence_detail: June SlopCodeBench Strict (n=3, mean): baseline 12.2, GSD 11.9, OMC 11.6, Superpowers-v5 11.4, Karpathy 11.1; spreads up to +/-2.3 exceed gaps. SWE-bench Pro June: baseline 52.80%, OMC 54.99, GSD 54.45, Superpowers-v5 54.17, Karpathy 53.08 (731 problems, single run).
cards.landing: A reason skills for greenfield or evidence-light work may cost attention; keep skills task-scoped and test them on SlopCodeBench-style long-horizon work.

cards.source_title: OrcaBot: Do Skills Improve Coding Agent Accuracy?
cards.author: other
cards.quote: It solves more checkpoints outright while breaking more of what it had already built.
cards.claim: Superpowers v6 led July SlopCodeBench Strict but had the worst Core and Partial scores, so its win is narrow and within noise.
cards.evidence_detail: July SlopCodeBench: Superpowers-v6 Strict 14.5 +/-2.3 vs baseline 13.9 +/-0.5; Core 62.6 vs 67.1; Partial 40.7 vs 46.3; erosion 0.46 vs 0.59; $/ckpt 1.71 vs 1.26.
cards.landing: Verifier design: score regression (erosion/Core) separately from outright solves; one headline pass rate hides breakage.

cards.source_title: OrcaBot: Do Skills Improve Coding Agent Accuracy?
cards.author: other
cards.quote: The single most important number on this page is the baseline's +2.76
cards.claim: The same model name and harness version improved by more than any skill pack's edge in one month (silent server-side drift), so one-off benchmark numbers decay and must be compared to a contemporaneous baseline.
cards.evidence_detail: Codex CLI v0.136.0, gpt-5.5 high, June to July: baseline SWE-bench Pro 52.80 to 55.56 (+2.76); SlopCodeBench Strict 12.2 to 13.9 (+1.7); verbosity 0.311 to 0.827. Karpathy pack (unchanged commit 2c60614) moved +3.44 and +1.8, tracking baseline.
cards.landing: Any effort-routing or verifier-config decision (including Dex's medium-vs-xhigh finding) should be re-measured periodically; pin or log model/harness versions in evidence folders.

cards.source_title: OrcaBot: Do Skills Improve Coding Agent Accuracy?
cards.author: other
cards.quote: the model got materially better at solving new checkpoints and no better at all at not breaking
cards.claim: Across both months erosion (regression of earlier checkpoints) stayed within +/-0.02 for every arm while Strict rose, and erosion looks like a property of the workflow, not the model.
cards.evidence_detail: Erosion June to July: baseline 0.58 to 0.59, Karpathy 0.58 to 0.58, Superpowers 0.46 to 0.46, GSD 0.54 to 0.53, OMC 0.52 to 0.54; no arm separates from baseline on per-checkpoint curves (cp1 about 75-81% down to 33-50% by cp8).
cards.landing: Supports gating on regression (pass-before/pass-after) rather than trusting prompts for discipline; a backpressure/verifier concern.

cards.source_title: OrcaBot: Do Skills Improve Coding Agent Accuracy?
cards.author: other
cards.quote: Every other pack buys its edge with 1.5-2x the tokens
cards.claim: Heavier skill packs cost 1.5-2x the tokens and dollars of baseline without a matching gain; the two most expensive arms lost to baseline in July.
cards.evidence_detail: July SWE-bench Pro tokens/problem and $/problem: baseline 1.37M/$0.37; Karpathy 1.37M/$0.37; Superpowers-v6 1.83M/$0.46; Agent Skills 2.07M/$0.52; OMC 2.19M/$0.53; GSD 2.70M/$0.61. SlopCodeBench $/ckpt: baseline 1.26, Karpathy 1.25, Superpowers 1.71, OMC 1.87, Agent Skills 2.00, GSD 2.02.
cards.landing: Cost-per-pass should be tracked when adding skills or routines; a short guideline pack (Karpathy) was the only one at baseline cost.

cards.source_title: OrcaBot: Do Skills Improve Coding Agent Accuracy?
cards.author: other
cards.quote: On a small task, it can compete with the actual specification for attention.
cards.claim: The authors hypothesise that skill instructions help on hard unfamiliar-repo tasks but compete with the spec on small or greenfield tasks, and that TDD-style skills presume visible tests and a reproducible bug.
cards.evidence_detail: Explanation offered, not tested: SWE-bench Pro has existing tests and regressions to use; SlopCodeBench keeps evaluator tests hidden and has no bug to reproduce.
cards.landing: Supports scoping skills and CLAUDE.md content by task type (load procedures only for brownfield work) and keeping per-phase context lean.

cards.source_title: OrcaBot: Do Skills Improve Coding Agent Accuracy?
cards.author: other
cards.quote: Because Codex is a single agent, multi-agent frameworks were applied as a single-agent sequential pass
cards.claim: Methodology caveat: all runs used Codex (not Claude), skills mounted read-only at pinned upstream commits, multi-agent packs flattened to one agent, SWE-bench Pro single seed with 30-minute cap, SlopCodeBench n=3.
cards.evidence_detail: Models: gpt-5.5 effort high via Codex CLI v0.136.0 in Docker; SWE-bench Pro public split 11 repos, 731 (June)/729 (July) instances; SlopCodeBench 36 problems/196 checkpoints, serial pytest; pack commits listed (GSD de73ad92 to 4fc89497, OMC a1720433 to 41a4c0f7, Superpowers v5.1.0 to v6, Karpathy 2c60614 both).
cards.landing: Limits how far the results transfer to Claude Code with sub-agents; note when citing against Dex's Claude-based SlopCodeBench report.

cards.source_title: OrcaBot: Do Skills Improve Coding Agent Accuracy?
cards.author: other
cards.quote: Any conclusion below about a pack, as opposed to the model, has a shelf life measured in weeks
cards.claim: Skill packs update faster than they can be evaluated: three of four moved past the tested commit within about two weeks, so a skill library needs re-measurement, not one-time vetting.
cards.evidence_detail: Checked 2026-08-07: GSD at a731a45, Agent Skills at d2478bf, Superpowers at 44c9b2d; only OMC still at its July commit. Pack updates conflate with drift (GSD +1.2 and OMC +0.5 Strict came in under drift of about +1.75).
cards.landing: If third-party skills are adopted, pin commits and re-run a fixed check; own saved workflows should carry a version and a re-test date.

cards.author: other
cards.quote: set up effective automated checks for linting, type checking, unit tests etc
cards.claim: Commenter says the codebase's automated checks beat tinkering with CLAUDE.md: if the agent repeats a mistake, add a lint rule or test instead.
cards.evidence_detail: andersco, no numbers; echoed by anonzzzies (drizzle sql templates ignored despite warnings), brianwawok (git lint hook; model lints randomly), philipp-gayret and MarkMarine (use hooks for must-happen rules).
cards.landing: Challenges prose rules in CLAUDE.md and the self-reported routine; argues for hook/lint enforcement (reopens the skipped hooks/pre-commit decision).
cards.inventory_ref: Writing a good CLAUDE.md (2025-11-25 blog; thread itself not listed)

cards.author: other
cards.quote: The solution is to simply have a bullet point in the CLAUDE.md file
cards.claim: Commenter defends short CLAUDE.md lines for norms a linter cannot catch (Mocha to Jest migration, convenience modules, getOne vs findOne), arguing prompts do work and an enforcement-only stance wastes tokens.
cards.evidence_detail: bastawhiz; reports it works for him and coworkers; counter from girvo that models still ignore the line sometimes so he re-checks manually.
cards.landing: Supports keeping a minimal always-loaded set of convention pointers while moving enforceable rules to checks.
cards.inventory_ref: Writing a good CLAUDE.md (2025-11-25 blog; thread itself not listed)

cards.author: other
cards.quote: they are all > 6 months old
cards.claim: Commenters note the instruction-count versus accuracy plot uses models more than six months old and doubt the steep decay holds for GPT 5.1, Gemini 3 or Claude 4.5.
cards.evidence_detail: jasonjmcghee and mmaunder; Kyle (0xblacklight) concedes the research is a few months old, has not been revisited, and conclusions about newer models cannot be drawn beyond what the post says; johnfn says Codex is the best rule-follower.
cards.landing: The 150-200 instruction and 'adherence falls at roughly 2x length' figures behind the CLAUDE.md trim are dated; verify on current models before trimming on that basis alone.
cards.inventory_ref: Writing a good CLAUDE.md (2025-11-25 blog; thread itself not listed)

cards.author: other
cards.quote: Doesn't that mean that Claude Code's system prompt exhausts that budget
cards.claim: A commenter points out the ~150-200 instruction budget is partly consumed by Claude Code's own system prompt (post says about 50), so a CLAUDE.md competes with it.
cards.evidence_detail: andai; self-corrects after noticing the post states the system prompt has 50 instructions.
cards.landing: Frames the CLAUDE.md length target as budget minus harness overhead, not an absolute line count.
cards.inventory_ref: Writing a good CLAUDE.md (2025-11-25 blog; thread itself not listed)

cards.author: other
cards.quote: Claude rarely actually reads the other documentation files I point it to.
cards.claim: Commenters report progressive disclosure via pointer docs is hit or miss because the agent does not reliably follow references; some add files to context manually or use skills.
cards.evidence_detail: sothatsit, Sammi, ffsm8 ('go for skills first'); vunderba and dimitri-vs say Skills are the codified version of a table-of-contents approach.
cards.landing: Pointer lists from a trimmed CLAUDE.md to docs/ need a trigger form or a skill with frontmatter; plain 'see docs' may not be followed.
cards.inventory_ref: Writing a good CLAUDE.md (2025-11-25 blog; thread itself not listed)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the key here is "if X then Y syntax"
cards.claim: Dex says writing pointers as 'if X then Y' conditions pierces the system-reminder's 'probably ignore this' framing by marking when an instruction is highly relevant.
cards.evidence_detail: dhorthy reply to sothatsit, 2025-12-01; no numbers.
cards.landing: Rewrite CLAUDE.md doc-map rows and skill descriptions as 'when doing X, read Y' triggers.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: injecting this file into the context window whenever an agent touches this directory
cards.claim: Dex says CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md differ from README because the harness injects them deterministically, and managing every token in and how it is presented beats relying on public training data.
cards.evidence_detail: dhorthy reply to _pdp_, 2025-11-30; argues for token-level context management in complex codebases.
cards.landing: Supports directory-scoped CLAUDE.md files (backend/, technician-app/) so root stays small.

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: you shouldn't use an LLM to do a linter & formatter's job
cards.claim: Post author Kyle says the durable principles are: don't make the LLM do a linter's job, LLMs are stateless and need onboarding, and deterministically injected instructions beat having the agent derive everything.
cards.evidence_detail: 0xblacklight; also says the post is 'how to use this config point right now', expects some advice to age poorly, and that it targets hard brownfield problems where /init output is rarely enough.
cards.landing: Pushes style/format rules out of CLAUDE.md into tooling; keep only non-derivable facts.
cards.inventory_ref: Writing a good CLAUDE.md (2025-11-25 blog; thread itself not listed)

cards.author: other
cards.quote: I removed all my instructions and it basically never violates those points.
cards.claim: A user says Opus 4.5 follows his coding-style preferences from reading the code alone, so he deleted his style instructions.
cards.evidence_detail: nurettin; also Zerot: conventions already in surrounding code make CLAUDE.md copies pure context cost.
cards.landing: Candidate trim: drop any rule the code or a linter already demonstrates; test by deleting and watching for violations.
cards.inventory_ref: Writing a good CLAUDE.md (2025-11-25 blog; thread itself not listed)

cards.author: other
cards.quote: The more context you give the lower it's upper end of quality becomes.
cards.claim: One commenter claims extra context and comments cap quality on hard problems and strips comments before sessions; others (xpe, Aurornis, stpedgwdgfhgdd) dispute generalising.
cards.evidence_detail: johnsmith1840 uses custom scripts, no controlled test; xpe reports ~10k tokens of guidelines in CLAUDE.md helped across conversations, also unmeasured.
cards.landing: Both directions are anecdote; supports measuring CLAUDE.md length effects in the knowledge-store pilot instead of assuming.
cards.inventory_ref: Writing a good CLAUDE.md (2025-11-25 blog; thread itself not listed)

cards.author: other
cards.quote: Mr Tinkleberry
cards.claim: A canary instruction (address me by a name) is used to detect when CLAUDE.md is no longer being followed; critics say it measures only the canary, and it may be ignored mid-conversation as low relevance.
cards.evidence_detail: nico, dkersten (emoji prefix), homeonthemtn ('Purple fish' picked and chosen); chickensong saw adherence at start/end but not middle; isoprophlex says the canary reinforces itself in context.
cards.landing: A cheap compliance signal for 'was the file loaded', but not proof rules were applied; relevant to telling skipped routine from unconsulted store.

cards.author: other
cards.quote: You could make a hook in Claude to re-inject claude.md.
cards.claim: Commenters propose hooks to re-inject CLAUDE.md or a /bootstrap command to reload it when the agent drifts, since it can be lost mid-session.
cards.evidence_detail: aqme28 (hook), jmathai (/bootstrap reading all CLAUDE.md, skills, commands; reports sessions not starting with them loaded), edf13 (proxy); Zerot says CLAUDE.md reloads on compaction.
cards.landing: Re-opens the skipped hooks decision for compaction recovery and compliance logging.

cards.author: other
cards.quote: CLAUDE.md should only be for persistent reminders that are useful in 100% of your sessions
cards.claim: Commenters say conditional content belongs in skills or subdirectory CLAUDE.md files that load on demand; but unshavedyak doubts skills reduce context if the agent loads them every time.
cards.evidence_detail: jswny, stingraycharles (src/persistence/CLAUDE.md auto-loaded when reading files there), vaer-k (cites Anthropic docs on child-directory CLAUDE.md), unshavedyak.
cards.landing: Concrete trim route for the 390-line file: move slice-specific invariants into backend/, technician-app/ CLAUDE.md or skills.
cards.inventory_ref: Writing a good CLAUDE.md (2025-11-25 blog; thread itself not listed)

cards.author: other
cards.quote: It seems to be 50/50 or LESS that Claude.md even reads/uses this file.
cards.claim: A heavy user reports CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md rules (e.g. method under 50 lines) are routinely ignored, so he re-pastes instructions after resetting context.
cards.evidence_detail: saberience; also AndyNemmity runs a very large but targeted CLAUDE.md with agents, hooks, skills and commands and says it works.
cards.landing: Adherence is contested; compliance cannot be assumed, supporting an external check for routine steps.

cards.author: other
cards.quote: If you're not benchmarking and systematically measuring the impact of your changes
cards.claim: A commenter says without benchmarking and systematic measurement, CLAUDE.md tuning is not prompt engineering, just improving by feel.
cards.evidence_detail: stingraycharles; related tsimionescu calls current practice closer to ritual than engineering; bird0861 notes prompts break on model changes ('prompt instability').
cards.landing: Supports gating a CLAUDE.md trim on a measured trial (P1 cold-resume) and re-testing after model updates.

cards.author: other
cards.quote: Work through lists and constantly update status so you can clear context
cards.claim: Commenters advise a short CLAUDE.md with pointers, status lists updated so context can be cleared and resumed, and one session per problem; also that Claude writes bloated CLAUDE.md files unless told one sentence per topic.
cards.evidence_detail: chickensong, aiibe ('one session for one problem', never hit context limit), handoflixue (instruct 'one sentence per topic, be concise'), dkersten (refresh context often).
cards.landing: Matches the one-phase-per-new-session routine and status-based resume; a concision instruction for agent-written docs.

gaps: The HN thread contains only comments; the blog post itself is not in this bundle (inventory lists it as Kyle's, 2025-11-25).
OrcaBot article cites Codex 5.5, not Claude, and never references Dex or his SlopCodeBench report directly; transfer to Claude Code is unmeasured.
OrcaBot charts (per-checkpoint curves) are only described in text; raw per-checkpoint data not in the file.
HN comment about CLAUDE.md length/adherence at 2x line count is not stated anywhere in the thread; only the 150-200 instruction figure (via andai) appears.
